[REFERENCE] N/A  
[RESPONSE] I’m not sure—I don’t recall noticing pain or stiffness specifically when rising from a seated position or after prolonged sitting.
[DIAGNOSIS] Pes anserine bursitis

[THOUGHT]  
The clinical summary presents a highly characteristic presentation of **pes anserine bursitis**: acute, localized, non-inflammatory medial knee pain just below the joint line in an active athlete with a clear overuse trigger (volleyball pivoting), focal tenderness at the classic anatomical location (~2–3 cm below the medial joint line), and absence of features suggesting alternative diagnoses (e.g., no joint line tenderness, no effusion, no mechanical symptoms, no radiographic abnormality). All supporting evidence aligns precisely with the diagnostic criteria for pes anserine bursitis — a superficial, overuse-related bursal inflammation. The exclusion of mimics is robust: fracture/dislocation ruled by X-ray; meniscal tear and patellofemoral pain syndrome ruled by absence of their hallmark signs/symptoms; osteoarthritis and stress fracture excluded by age/activity profile and lack of progressive or night pain and bony tenderness. Ultrasound is appropriately recommended as the optimal confirmatory test given its high sensitivity for superficial bursal fluid and thickening. No contradictory or confounding findings are present.

[EVIDENCE]  
• Acute onset (1 day) of localized medial tibial pain just inferior to the patella  
• Pain located specifically ~2–3 cm below the medial joint line — classic pes anserine bursa location  
• Temporal association with increased volleyball activity involving repetitive pivoting/twisting (known risk factor for pes anserine bursitis)  
• Absence of trauma, swelling, erythema, warmth, or joint effusion (confirmed on X-ray)  
• No weight-bearing impairment — consistent with isolated bursal irritation, not intra-articular or osseous pathology  
• Positive focal tenderness *only* over the pes anserine bursa (no joint line tenderness, no patellar tenderness)  
• Negative X-ray (AP, lateral, sunrise views) excluding fracture, dislocation, and degenerative changes  
• No mechanical symptoms (locking, catching) — argues against meniscal tear  
• No pain with stair climbing, squatting, or rising from sitting — inconsistent with patellofemoral pain syndrome  
• No stiffness after rest — argues against osteoarthritis  

[GAPS]  
None  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Pes anserine bursitis
